body:
How Long Is It?: 1. Right at the end of the object (with no space before the first clip). 2. Gaps leave parts that are not counted, so the number would be wrong (too small). 3. The marker (6 is more than 4). 4. Answers vary; the cubes line up from heel to toe with no gaps or overlaps and the number matches.
Measure and Compare: 1. The ribbon; 3 cubes longer. 2. The red snake is the longest; the green snake is the shortest. 3. Pencil, door, bus. 4. Answers vary; the drawing shows cubes end to end with no gaps or overlaps and the number matches the drawing. 5. Lee's 9 is right. Ava's gaps left parts of the book that she did not count, so her number is too small.
Clocks and Charts: 1. 3:00 (3 o'clock). 2. 7:30 (half past 7). 3. Short hand on 9, long hand on 12. 4. Short hand halfway between 4 and 5, long hand on 6. 5. Eleven thirty, or half past eleven. 6. 3 more children (8 - 5). 7. 16 children (5 + 8 + 3).
Measuring and Time Check: 1. The shoe. 2. Longer. 3. Drawing shows 5 cubes end to end, the same length as the pencil, with no gaps or overlaps. 4. 10:00 (10 o'clock). 5. Short hand halfway between 2 and 3, long hand on 6. 6. Sunny. 7. 2 more votes (9 - 7); 20 children voted (9 + 4 + 7).
Scoring tip: for half hours, a short hand drawn pointing exactly at 2 for 2:30 is Getting there; the hour hand should sit halfway between 2 and 3. For the snake and rope problems, accept a drawing that shows the order as the explanation.
title: Answer key: Measuring and Telling Time
